The observable change is the required correction for translated Git outside repositories. English behavior, return types, serialized contracts and ordinary diagnostic languages remain compatible.
The two new tests fail without both production changes in C and pt_BR; the upstream pair fails only in pt_BR before the fix. All four and the full suites pass after restoration.

Intent, R1, R2, D1 and the changelog match the two production edits and the four regression scenarios. No operational scaffold behavior or user command changes require a template migration.
A genuine non-repository again reports missing releases rather than unreadable Git in Portuguese. Damaged .git ancestors remain uncertain, and non-probe Git diagnostics keep the user language.
Current sealed locale integration evidence exercises R1 directly and R2 through ResolveReleaseTag and both upstream release consumers; independent bilingual runs corroborate it.
